efficacy.magnitude_basis: co-primary LDL-C % change vs placebo at week 4: +0.2 % (P=0.93) against the niacin-like -10 to -20 % the FFA hypothesis implied; HDL-C co-primary +4.6 % (P=0.013) vs niacin's ~15-25 %

patient_trials.quote: Percent Change From Baseline in LDL-C (week 4): MK1903 -0.3 (SD 16.3), Placebo -1.5 (SD 12.9); mean difference 0.2 (95% CI -3.9 to 4.3), P=0.926.
Change From Baseline in Direct LDL-C at Week 8: SCH 900271 15 mg -2.0, 10 mg -1.5, 5 mg -4.2, 2.5 mg 0.2, 1 mg 1.2, Placebo 1.5; 15 mg vs placebo -3.5 (P=0.06).

efficacy.reason: Weak lipid effect versus niacin, abandoned
efficacy.judgement: Dated 2012 because MK-1903's own rat datum was public only with Boatman (Apr 2012); a reader pairing the sibling-based rat prediction (Shen 2009) with the 2010 registry posting would date it 2010, still contra. Scored on the LDL-C co-primary as the draft does on its other tracks; HDL-C +4.6 % and TG -10.3 % moved in the predicted direction but below the niacin bar, and the sponsor abandoned both members.

safety.model: Gpr109a (PUMA-G) knockout vs wild-type mouse, plasma FFA / flushing
safety.note: Knockout mouse showed niacin flushing is GPR109A-mediated: the model predicts on-target flushing from any full agonist. Opener on the SCH 900271 track: knockout dosed with niacin, dated at the model's first use as a proxy.
safety.quote: In the present study, we show that mice lacking PUMA-G did not show nicotinic acid-induced flushing.
safety.judgement: Same mouse system as the FFA track (same model_id); the flushing readout entered in 2005. Prediction: full agonists flush. MK-0354, the partial agonist that did not flush in mice or humans, is class context only and not scored.

safety.model: Gpr109a (PUMA-G) knockout vs wild-type mouse, plasma FFA / flushing
safety.note: As the mouse predicted, the full agonist SCH 900271 flushed patients dose-dependently: 17 % at 15 mg versus 2 % on placebo.
safety.short: Full agonist flushed patients, as predicted
safety.confidence_note: Registry AE table row, not prose. MK-1903's registry (NCT00847197) lists only SOC-level 'vascular disorders' 42/116 vs 8/75 placebo and 'skin disorders' 32/116 vs 2/75, so the MK-1903 flushing term cannot be quoted; Lauring 2012 Table S2 was not accessible.
safety.judgement: Paired by me: Benyo 2005 (mouse) vs the SCH 900271 phase 2 AE table. The on-target harm the knockout mouse predicted appeared in patients; magnitude is direction only because the mouse gives no incidence.

safety.model: Fasted beagle dog, plasma FFA and flushing
safety.note: Dog: no overt flushing to 10 mg/kg, ten times the FFA ED50, an improved window over nicotinic acid.
safety.quote: Compound 33 had no overt signs of flushing at doses up to 10 mg/kg with an improved therapeutic window to flushing as compared to nicotinic acid.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract only; the flushing species is read as the dog from context.

safety.model: Fasted beagle dog, plasma FFA and flushing
safety.note: Patients flushed dose-dependently (17 % at 15 mg) but far below niacin's rates; the dog's 'improved window' held, its 'no overt flushing' did not.
safety.short: Wider window than niacin, not flush-free
safety.confidence_note: Registry AE row. No niacin comparator in the trial; 'far below niacin' rests on general knowledge of extended-release niacin flushing rates, not on a source in this entry. The human FFA-effective dose is not in the abstract, so the human window cannot be computed.
safety.magnitude_basis: flushing incidence vs niacin's typical rates; no in-trial niacin arm
safety.judgement: Judgement call: partial match rather than contra. The stated prediction had two parts; the comparative one (better window than nicotinic acid) is consistent with 17 % at the top dose, the absolute one (no overt flushing) was contradicted at 10-15 mg. Low confidence because the human window is unquantified.

safety.note: Guinea pig ear-temperature model predicted minimal flushing for GSK256073.
safety.quote: A guinea pig model was used to predict flushing, via an increase in ear temperature, and GSK256073 was found to have a minimal effect in this model.
safety.judgement: A different system (guinea pig ear temperature) and a different prediction (no flush at NEFA-effective exposure) from the knockout mouse, so its own track.

safety.note: GSK authors: the guinea pig flush model predicted the human response; FTIH NEFA lowering came without flushing in healthy men. Retrodiction ruling: GSK256073's own patient result, no flushing in type 2 diabetes (Dobbins 2013, June 2013), was public before this 2015 model paper, so the match is retro.
safety.short: No flushing in FTIH, as guinea pig predicted
safety.quote: These preclinical models appeared to be predictive of human response, since in a first-time-in-human study, GSK256073 displayed long lasting NEFA and triglyceride lowering effects in healthy male subjects, which were not associated with flushing.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading only (full text paywalled). FTIH NCT not found.
safety.magnitude_basis: flushing absent at NEFA-lowering doses, direction only
safety.judgement: Comparison stated by the source. Diabetes trials (Dobbins 2013, 2015: 'not associated with events of flushing'; safety 'did not significantly differ from placebo') agree but are another indication and not scored.

safety.note: Dyslipidaemic patients: no excess flushing at the NEFA-effective 5 and 50 mg (4/19, 5/20 vs 5/21 placebo); excess only at 150 mg (12/20). Retrodiction ruling: the model paper (2015) post-dates the drug's own no-flush patient result (Dobbins 2013), so retro.
safety.short: No excess flush at effective doses
safety.quote: Flushing: GSK256073 5 mg 4/19; 50 mg 5/20; 150 mg 12/20; Placebo 5/21.
safety.confidence_note: Registry AE row; small arms (19-21 per group). Self-reported flushing diaries in the same record show more episodes at 150 mg.
safety.magnitude_basis: flushing AE incidence by dose vs placebo
safety.reason: Flush models right at effective doses
safety.judgement: Strengthens the 2015 same with patient data. Partial: flushing did appear at 150 mg, 15-30 times the NEFA-effective dose (10 mg QD suppressed NEFA fully in Dobbins 2013), which I read as a margin detail rather than a failed prediction; a stricter reader could call it contra at the top dose.

safety.model: Wild-type mouse dermal blood-flow (vasodilation / flushing) model after oral agonist, Merck
safety.note: Mouse vasodilation model predicts on-target flushing and ranks agonists by their window over niacin; no member in patients yet.
safety.short: Mouse flush window, no patients yet
safety.quote: Compound 2i exhibited good in vivo antilipolytic efficacy while providing a significantly improved therapeutic index over vasodilation (flushing) with respect to niacin in the mouse model.

safety.model: Wild-type mouse dermal blood-flow (vasodilation / flushing) model after oral agonist, Merck
safety.note: Mouse predicted MK-1903 flushes (+30 % dermal blood flow); patients had vascular events 36 % vs 11 %, skin events 28 % vs 3 %. Retrodiction ruling: MK-1903's own patient AE rows (posted 2010-09-22) predate its mouse dermal-flow datum (April 2012), so retro.
safety.short: MK-1903 flushed patients as mouse predicted
safety.quote: Vascular disorders: MK1903 42/116, Placebo 8/75; Skin and subcutaneous tissue disorders: MK1903 32/116, Placebo 2/75.
safety.confidence_note: Registry rows are system-organ-class counts without the term flushing; Lauring 2012 Tables S2/S3 (MK-1903 AEs) and the Offermanns 2012 Focus sentence that MK-1903 'produced a flushing response similar to that of nicotinic acid' could not be read, so whether the mouse's window over niacin held is unverified.
safety.magnitude_basis: mouse dermal blood flow +30 % vs patient vascular/skin adverse-event incidence; no common scale, and the mouse gives no incidence
safety.judgement: Paired by me: Boatman 2012 mouse (+30 % dermal blood flow, via Tuteja & Duffy 2016) vs NCT00847197 AE rows. Direction held: the model said MK-1903 flushes and patients flushed. If Lauring's Table S2 or the Offermanns Focus shows niacin-like flushing against a mouse claim of a reduced window, this becomes same + partial (window misplaced) on the dog track's pattern; not readable here.
